root_cause.text: Bluetooth socket destructors in the HCI/ISO/L2CAP/SCO paths failed to purge `sk->sk_error_queue`, so TX timestamping SKBs queued by `SO_TIMESTAMPING` could remain referenced and leak when the socket was destroyed or the controller disappeared.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `skb_queue_purge(&sk->sk_error_queue);` to `hci_sock_destruct()`, `iso_sock_destruct()`, `l2cap_sock_destruct()`, and `sco_sock_destruct()`, and the CVE text says “SKBs may be queued into sk_error_queue and will stay there until consumed” and “Fix by adding skb_queue_purge() calls for sk_error_queue in affected bluetooth destructors.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Purge the socket error queue during HCI socket destruction to clean up all queued packets and avoid resource leakage.
intent_record.what: In hci_sock_destruct(), an additional call to skb_queue_purge(&sk->sk_error_queue) was added after the existing purges of sk_receive_queue and sk_write_queue.
intent_record.how: When an HCI socket is destroyed, its error queue is now also emptied, ensuring any queued error sk_buffs are released and preventing leftover error messages or memory from persisting after socket teardown.

intent_record.intent_summary: Purge the ISO socket error queue during destruction to prevent leftover queued errors and resource leaks.
intent_record.what: In iso_sock_destruct(), a new call to skb_queue_purge(&sk->sk_error_queue) was added after the existing purges of sk_receive_queue and sk_write_queue.
intent_record.how: When an ISO socket is destroyed, its error queue is now also emptied, ensuring any queued error skbs are released instead of lingering after socket teardown and potentially leaking resources.

intent_record.intent_summary: Purge the socket error queue during L2CAP socket destruction to ensure complete cleanup.
intent_record.what: In l2cap_sock_destruct(), a new call to skb_queue_purge(&sk->sk_error_queue) was added immediately after the existing purges of sk_receive_queue and sk_write_queue.
intent_record.how: When an L2CAP socket is destroyed, any packets or messages queued on the socket's error queue are now freed as part of teardown, preventing them from being left behind during socket cleanup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Purge the SCO socket error queue during destruction to ensure complete cleanup and prevent stale queued errors or leaks.
intent_record.what: In `sco_sock_destruct(struct sock *sk)`, a new call to `skb_queue_purge(&sk->sk_error_queue);` was added after the existing purges of `sk_receive_queue` and `sk_write_queue`.
intent_record.how: When a SCO socket is destroyed, its error queue is now explicitly emptied as well, preventing any leftover queued error sk_buffs from persisting past socket teardown and avoiding associated resource leaks or stale state.

relevance_review.reason: The changes explicitly purge the socket error queue during Bluetooth socket destruction in the ISO/HCI paths, which matches the root cause of leaked TX timestamping SKBs remaining in sk_error_queue after socket teardown.

The root cause is failure to purge sk->sk_error_queue in Bluetooth socket destructors, causing leaked timestamping SKBs. This group explicitly adds error-queue purging during L2CAP socket destruction, directly addressing the vulnerability.
The change explicitly purges the SCO socket error queue during destruction, which matches the root cause of missing sk_error_queue cleanup causing timestamping SKBs to leak.

candidates.rationale: This destructor path cleans only the receive and write queues; the root cause is that sk->sk_error_queue was not purged, allowing timestamping SKBs to remain referenced after socket teardown.
The ISO socket cleanup path shows the pre-fix destructor only purged receive/write queues, leaving sk->sk_error_queue uncleared and causing leaked queued errors/SKBs.
This is part of the L2CAP socket destruction cleanup that omitted purging sk->sk_error_queue, which is the vulnerable condition described in the root cause.
The SCO destructor only purged receive/write queues before the fix; failing to purge sk->sk_error_queue let error-queue SKBs survive socket destruction.

vuln_statements.explanation: In the HCI socket destructor, only the receive queue was purged. The missing purge of sk->sk_error_queue allowed TX timestamping SKBs to remain referenced after socket teardown.
In the ISO socket destructor, this cleanup only handled the receive queue and did not purge sk->sk_error_queue, leaving error-queue SKBs behind.
In the L2CAP socket destructor, the cleanup omitted sk->sk_error_queue, so queued timestamping/error SKBs could leak when the socket was destroyed.
In the SCO socket destructor, only the receive queue was purged. The absence of a sk->sk_error_queue purge caused the vulnerability by leaving queued SKBs referenced.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is the failure to purge socket queues at socket destruction time, especially the error/queued SKBs after the socket is no longer referenced. In this snippet, the old purge calls are removed from hci_sock_release(): 'skb_queue_purge(&sk->sk_receive_queue);' and 'skb_queue_purge(&sk->sk_write_queue);' are deleted there, but the fix is added by introducing 'static void hci_sock_destruct(struct sock *sk)' that purges those queues, and by setting 'sk->sk_destruct = hci_sock_destruct;' in hci_sock_create(). This means the code already contains the corrective handling that moves queue purging to destruct time. Also, this specific snippet does not show the error queue ('sk->sk_error_queue') mentioned in the root cause, so the exact vulnerable construct is not present here.
